summary_en: Mariken Lease changed its dividend policy to introduce progressive dividends for the remaining period of the current medium-term plan (FY2027-FY2029), committing to maintain or increase annual dividends. The company raised FY2027 full-year dividend forecast to 57 yen per share from 54 yen, reflecting a 3 yen increase in the final dividend.
title_en: Notice Regarding Change in Dividend Policy (Introduction of Progressive Dividends) and Revision of Full-Year Dividend Forecast for FY2027 (Increase in Dividend)
translation_en_brief:
On November 6, 2026, Mariken Lease's Board of Directors approved a change to its dividend policy and a revision to its FY2027 dividend forecast. The company will introduce progressive dividends (annual basis) for the remainder of its current medium-term plan spanning FY2027 through FY2029, committing to maintain or increase annual dividend payments in principle, while maintaining a dividend payout ratio of 35 percent or higher on a consolidated basis.

For FY2027, the company raised its full-year dividend forecast to 57 yen per share from the previously announced 54 yen. This represents a 3 yen increase in the final dividend from 27 yen to 30 yen (interim dividend remains unspecified). The revision follows four consecutive years of dividend increases from FY2023 through FY2026. Note that the company executed a 1-for-3 stock split on April 1, 2026; FY2027 figures reflect post-split amounts. On a pre-split basis, the annual dividend would be 171 yen.

The policy change formalizes the company's commitment to shareholder returns. By explicitly introducing progressive dividends—a framework that rules out dividend cuts and commits to maintenance or growth—management aims to provide greater clarity on capital allocation during the final years of the current medium-term plan.
